headline: Readable names and C data make the completed decompilation easier to work on
summary: Contributors can navigate source by system, use named buttons, levels and hero states, and share declarations instead of maintaining local copies. Code remains 100.00% matched: 3,713,096 bytes and all 5,116 functions compile to the original game's bytes; the brief does not identify a disc version. Compiled data reaches 73.94%, with values generated locally from each contributor's disc rather than committed. The 231,369 added and 208,167 removed lines largely reflect formatting: #169 alone added 169,328 and removed 147,550.
highlights: Data blocks and pointer references now build from C, while checks preserve the existing function matches (#196, #197, #198).
Tools can reject or revert refactors that break matching; CI checks syntax, lint and tools, while disc-dependent matching stays local (#168, #204).
Unnecessary matching tricks were removed and necessary ones documented; unresolved syntax conflicts remain (#195, #200, #201, #202).
Level extraction issue #165 closed as completed after reporting an out-of-range ISO read.
